proposed_statement_changes.reason: The displayed asymptotic simplifications require \(\ell_n/n_\ast\to0\). With \(\delta\) allowed to approach zero arbitrarily fast, no threshold independent of \(\delta\) ensures even \(h_n<1\); fixing \(\delta\) and allowing the threshold to depend on it is the honest scope supported by the rate calculation.
The packing choice and the limit \(\chi^2\to0\) prove the separation bound for all sufficiently large \(n_\ast\). The current unqualified conclusion omits that limit condition.

The comparison \(\log(C_0Rn_\ast/0.05)\lesssim\log n_\ast\) is valid only for sufficiently large \(n_\ast\), and the original right-hand side is zero at \(n_\ast=1\). The explicit asymptotic qualifier is necessary.

An operator-norm Hessian band of radius \(r_{H,n}\) does not make the entrywise box obtained by independently enlarging every entry by \(r_{H,n}\) an equally tight operator-norm uncertainty set: already in dimension two, the entrywise box contains \(r_{H,n}\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}\), whose operator norm is \(2r_{H,n}\). Moreover, negativity of the factual-coordinate field \(\widehat S_{pq}\) need not give a fixed source direction robust to that larger box. The proposed source-product trigger and the explicit scalar perturbation allowance are sufficient for a terminating certified chord.

proposed_definition_changes.reason: The current procedure multiplies independently enlarged entrywise intervals, losing the operator-norm geometry that justifies \(w_n\); its strict \(\widehat\gamma_{pq}+w_n<0\) trigger therefore does not imply interval termination. The corrected construction tests the symmetric source-product field and adds the rigorously derived scalar error \((2M+r_{H,n})r_{H,n}t_{\mathrm{ch}}^2\lVert z\rVert_2^2\).
